# Temple Scroll Column 64 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 64 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**64:1** You shall not neglect the Levite who resides within your gates, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.

**64:2** At the end of every three years you shall bring out the full tithe of your produce for that year and store it within your gates.

**64:3** The Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance with you, together with the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow within your gates, shall come and eat their fill,

**64:4** so that I may bless you in all the work of your hands.

**64:5** At the end of every seven years you shall grant a release. This is the manner of the release: every creditor shall release the claim he holds against his neighbor. He shall not press his neighbor or his brother for payment,

**64:6** for the release of the LORD has been proclaimed. From a foreigner you may exact payment, but whatever claim you hold against your brother, your hand shall release.

**64:7** If a man is found kidnapping any of his brothers from among the children of Israel, and he enslaves him or sells him, that kidnapper shall die. So you shall purge the evil from your midst.

**64:8** If a man has committed a crime deserving the sentence of death, and he is executed, and you hang him on a tree,

**64:9** his body shall not remain on the tree overnight. You shall bury him that same day, for one who is hanged is accursed of God.

**64:10** You shall not defile your land, which I am giving you as an inheritance.

**64:11** If a man acts as an informer against his people, delivering his people to a foreign nation and working evil against his people,

**64:12** you shall hang him on a tree so that he dies. By the testimony of two witnesses or by the testimony of three witnesses

**64:13** he shall be put to death, and they shall hang him on the tree.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Column 64 is the theological crux of the Temple Scroll. The council carefully distinguished two hanging laws: (1) 64:8–10 follows Deuteronomy — post-mortem display after execution, with mandatory same-day burial; (2) 64:11–13 is the Temple Scroll's innovation — hanging alive as the method of execution for treason. LOGOS's "so that he dies" captures the crucial difference. "Sojourner" (EMET) preferred over "resident alien" (LOGOS) or "foreigner" (PNEUMA) for גר. "Informer" (LOGOS) preferred over PNEUMA's "spy" as closer to רכל. "Accursed of God" preserves the genitive ambiguity that was so theologically productive in both Jewish and Christian interpretation.*
